stages.name: Persian Empire
stages.desc: Achaemenid satrapies and subject kings, before Alexander

stages.name: Macedon & Antigonids
stages.desc: Alexander, then Antigonus, Demetrius and the Antigonid kings of Macedon

stages.name: Ptolemaic
stages.desc: The Ptolemies, Macedonian kings of Egypt ruling from Alexandria

stages.name: Seleucid
stages.desc: The Seleucids, Macedonian kings of Syria and Asia

stages.name: Carthaginian
stages.desc: Carthage, the great Phoenician city of Africa

stages.name: Rome & its allies
stages.desc: Roman provinces, client states and allies

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Cyprus's city-kingdoms, among them Phoenician Kition, are subjects of Persia
The Cypriot kings go over to Alexander and send ships to the siege of Tyre
Ptolemy takes the island and puts to death Pumiathon, the last Phoenician king of Kition
Demetrius wins the sea battle off Salamis; Cyprus passes to the Antigonids
Ptolemy recovers Cyprus, which stays Ptolemaic for more than two centuries
Antiochus IV briefly occupies Cyprus, then withdraws at Rome's demand

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon, Byblos and Arwad are Phoenician city-kingdoms under Persia
Alexander takes Tyre after a seven-month siege; Sidon and Byblos had opened their gates
Ptolemy seizes Syria and the Phoenician coast
Antigonus takes the coast and besieges Tyre for fifteen months
Ptolemy's fleet takes Tyre and Sidon from Demetrius
Antiochus III overruns Phoenicia
After the battle of Raphia the coast returns to Ptolemy IV
Antiochus III wins at Panium; Phoenicia becomes Seleucid

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Persian satrapies; in spring Alexander crosses the Hellespont and wins at the Granicus
After Issus, Asia Minor belongs to Alexander
Antigonus falls at Ipsus; Lysimachus takes most of Asia Minor
Seleucus defeats Lysimachus at Corupedium
Treaty of Apamea: Rome gives Seleucid Asia Minor to its allies Pergamon and Rhodes

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage rules the coast and farmland of present-day Tunisia
Agathocles of Syracuse lands in Africa and ravages Carthage's lands
The Spartan Xanthippus leads Carthage to victory over the Roman invader Regulus
Defeated at sea, Carthage faces the revolt of its unpaid mercenaries
Hannibal is beaten at Zama; Carthage loses its fleet and overseas empire
Rome destroys Carthage and creates the province of Africa

states.name: Greece
timeline: Macedon rules Greece through the League of Corinth; Antipater is Alexander's regent
Athens loses the Lamian War and receives a Macedonian garrison
Demetrius drives out Cassander's governor and 'frees' Athens
Antigonus Gonatas secures the throne of Macedon
Athens surrenders to Gonatas at the end of the Chremonidean War
Rome defeats Perseus at Pydna and abolishes the Macedonian kingdom
Rome sacks Corinth; Macedonia becomes a province whose governor oversees Greece

states.name: Egypt
timeline: A Persian satrapy, reconquered by Artaxerxes III in 343 BC
Egypt surrenders to Alexander without a fight
Ptolemy takes Egypt as satrap; he will crown himself king in 305 BC
The priests' decree of Memphis, copied on the Rosetta Stone, honours Ptolemy V
A Roman envoy turns Antiochus IV back from Alexandria

events.title: The Granicus
events.text: Alexander crosses the Hellespont and defeats the Persian satraps at the river Granicus.

events.title: Zeno is born
events.text: Zeno, son of Mnaseas, is born in Kition, a Phoenician city-kingdom on Cyprus.

events.title: Battle of Issus
events.text: Alexander defeats Darius III, opening the road to Phoenicia and Egypt.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: Tyre falls after seven months; thousands are killed and some thirty thousand sold into slavery.

events.title: Alexandria founded
events.text: Alexander founds a new city on the Egyptian coast.

events.title: Ptolemy takes Egypt
events.text: After Alexander's death in Babylon, his general Ptolemy takes Egypt as his share.

events.title: Athens loses its freedom
events.text: Defeated in the Lamian War, Athens receives a Macedonian garrison in Piraeus.

events.title: Antigonus besieges Tyre
events.text: Antigonus the One-Eyed lays a fifteen-month siege to Tyre.

events.title: Kition's last king
events.text: Ptolemy has Pumiathon of Kition killed, ending the city's Phoenician dynasty.

events.title: The shipwreck
events.text: Zeno, a merchant carrying purple dye, is said to be wrecked off Piraeus and stays in Athens.

events.title: Agathocles in Africa
events.text: The tyrant of Syracuse lands at Cap Bon and wars in Carthage's own hinterland.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.text: Demetrius destroys Ptolemy's fleet off Cyprus; Antigonus and Demetrius take the title of king.

events.title: Siege of Rhodes
events.text: Demetrius 'the Besieger' fails to take Rhodes after a year.

events.title: Battle of Ipsus
events.text: Antigonus is killed; his rivals divide his Asian empire.

events.title: The Painted Porch
events.text: Zeno begins teaching in the Stoa Poikile, a public colonnade on the Agora; his followers are called Stoics.

events.title: Ptolemaic Phoenicia
events.text: Ptolemy's fleet takes Tyre and Sidon; Philocles, king of Sidon, serves him as admiral.

events.title: Corupedium
events.text: Seleucus defeats and kills Lysimachus, winning Asia Minor.

events.title: Gauls at Delphi
events.text: Celtic invaders sweep through Macedonia and attack Delphi.

events.title: Persaeus goes to Pella
events.text: Zeno, invited by King Antigonus Gonatas, sends his pupil Persaeus of Kition in his place.

events.title: Chremonidean War
events.text: Athens and Sparta, backed by Ptolemy II, rise against Macedon.

events.title: First Punic War
events.text: Rome and Carthage go to war over Messana in Sicily.

events.title: Zeno dies
events.text: Athens votes Zeno a golden crown and a public tomb; Cleanthes of Assos succeeds him.

events.title: Regulus defeated
events.text: Xanthippus defeats the Roman invasion army near Tunis.

events.title: Fall of Acrocorinth
events.text: Aratus seizes Corinth's citadel; its commander Persaeus is killed.

events.title: Mercenary War
events.text: Carthage's unpaid mercenaries revolt; the war lasts more than three years.

events.title: Chrysippus leads
events.text: Chrysippus of Soli in Cilicia succeeds Cleanthes and systematises Stoicism.

events.title: Athens buys freedom
events.text: Athens pays the Macedonian commander to withdraw his garrison from Piraeus.

events.title: Hannibal's War
events.text: Hannibal marches on Italy; the Second Punic War begins.

events.title: Battle of Raphia
events.text: Ptolemy IV defeats Antiochus III and keeps Phoenicia.

events.title: Battle of Zama
events.text: Scipio defeats Hannibal; Carthage gives up its fleet and empire.

events.title: Battle of Panium
events.text: Antiochus III takes Phoenicia and Coele-Syria from the Ptolemies.

events.title: Freedom of the Greeks
events.text: At the Isthmian Games, the Roman Flamininus proclaims the Greeks free.

events.title: Rosetta decree
events.text: Egyptian priests honour Ptolemy V in a decree later copied on the Rosetta Stone.

events.title: Peace of Apamea
events.text: Defeated at Magnesia, Antiochus III gives up Asia Minor to Rome's allies.

events.title: Hasdrubal is born
events.text: In Carthage a boy is born who will become the philosopher Clitomachus.

events.title: Battle of Pydna
events.text: Rome destroys the Macedonian phalanx; the last Antigonid king is led in triumph.

events.title: Day of Eleusis
events.text: The Roman envoy Popillius draws a circle round Antiochus IV and orders him out of Egypt.

events.title: A Carthaginian in Athens
events.text: Hasdrubal comes to Athens, takes the name Clitomachus and studies under Carneades.

events.title: Philosophers' embassy
events.text: Carneades of the Academy and the Stoic Diogenes of Babylon lecture in Rome.

events.title: Third Punic War
events.text: Rome declares war and lays siege to Carthage.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: Scipio Aemilianus storms Carthage; the survivors are enslaved and the city is burned.

events.title: Corinth sacked
events.text: Mummius sacks Corinth; Greece passes under Roman rule.

events.title: A consolation
events.text: Clitomachus writes a consolation to his captive countrymen, drawn from Carneades' teaching.

eras: The Fall of Carthage and Corinth
chartNote: Share of the area of six present-day countries (Greece, Turkey, Cyprus, Lebanon, Egypt and Tunisia), by the power that held most of each; regions are today's boundaries. A simplification: borders shifted constantly, Lysimachus's Asia Minor (301–281 BC) is shown with the Macedonian kings, and Pergamon and Rhodes after 188 BC with Rome's allies. Turkey and Egypt dominate the shares.
